body_markdown:
## **TL;DR**


- For occasional founder signatures, choose a lightweight standalone tool such as Dropbox Sign or SignNow.
- For sales documents that require built-in creation and proposal workflows, consider PandaDoc.
- For hiring documents, DocuSign or Adobe Acrobat Sign may fit established document workflows. Zoho Sign suits startups already using Zoho.
- For reusable agreements, internal approvals, structured contract data, and ongoing management,[Common Paper](https://commonpaper.com/) connects signatures to the full contract lifecycle.
- Match the product to your document volume and workflow. Compare plan-level pricing, usage limits, integrations, and contract management features before buying.


## **What startups actually need from e-signature software**


Your signing needs usually expand as your startup handles more contracts. A founder signing an occasional NDA or financing document may only need to upload a PDF, place signature fields, and download the completed copy. For this use case, ease of use and low cost often matter more than templates or integrations.


Repeatable sales contracts require more control. Reusable templates reduce manual edits, while signer ordering, automated reminders, and status tracking keep agreements moving. CRM integrations become useful when sales representatives need to send approved documents without copying customer details between tools.


Hiring paperwork creates a different workflow. Offer letters, confidentiality agreements, and contractor documents may require multiple signers and careful handling of personal information. An audit trail should record who opened and signed each document, along with the relevant timestamps and authentication details.


Startup-wide contract operations extend beyond signatures. When legal, finance, or security must review an agreement, you may need internal approval routing, version control, structured contract data, and records of negotiated changes. You may also need to track renewal dates and obligations after both parties sign.


A standalone e-signature tool fits when your documents arrive ready for execution and you mainly need signatures, reminders, and records. Contract management software fits when you also need to create reusable agreements, manage reviews, route approvals, and use contract data in other business systems. Contract management software becomes useful when recurring agreements require review by people in sales, legal, finance, or security, or when someone must track contract terms after signature.

## **DocuSign**


DocuSign suits startups that need extensive integrations, administrative controls, or signing workflows that connect with software already used by larger customers. Its broad integration catalog connects signing with common CRM, productivity, and storage tools. DocuSign provides compliance documentation and administrative controls, but buyers should confirm that the required certifications and controls are available for their product and plan.


Smaller startups may find that breadth adds cost and setup work they do not need. A founder sending occasional PDFs may prefer a simpler tool with fewer configuration choices. Before buying, check whether the selected plan includes the required templates, reminders, integrations, signer limits, and administrative features. DocuSign reserves some capabilities for higher-priced plans.


Choose DocuSign when enterprise customers request it, your company needs several business systems connected to signing, or administrators require detailed control over users and workflows. A lightweight e-signature product will usually fit better when you only need to upload documents, place fields, collect signatures, and retain an audit trail. Startups that also need reusable agreements, internal approvals, structured contract data, and renewal tracking should compare DocuSign’s broader contract products with dedicated contract management software.


## **PandaDoc**


PandaDoc fits sales-heavy startups that want to create proposals and collect signatures in one workflow. Its document editor lets you assemble branded proposals, reuse templates, and add pricing information without preparing every document in Word or PDF first. Sales representatives can prepare and send customer-facing documents in the same editor instead of formatting each proposal in a separate Word or PDF file.


PandaDoc also supports electronic signatures, recipient tracking, reminders, and common sales integrations. Those features suit repeatable sales workflows where representatives need to see whether a prospect has opened or signed a document. Startups that mainly send polished proposals may find this approach more useful than a basic tool built around uploading finished PDFs.


PandaDoc places less emphasis on contract lifecycle management than a dedicated contract platform. A startup that needs internal approval rules, structured contract data, or ongoing obligation tracking should compare those requirements carefully. PandaDoc is a suitable option when the buyer prioritizes proposal creation and sales presentation alongside electronic signatures.


## **Adobe Acrobat Sign**


Adobe Acrobat Sign fits companies whose contracts already move through PDF, Acrobat, and Microsoft business applications. You can prepare a PDF in an Adobe workflow, place signature and form fields, and send the document without rebuilding it in a separate document editor.


Adobe Acrobat Sign may reduce application switching for employees who prepare and route documents through Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, or Dynamics 365. A sales or hiring workflow can keep documents close to the applications employees already use, which reduces file transfers and duplicate data entry. Available integrations and automation features vary by plan, so buyers should confirm packaging against their current software stack.


Acrobat Sign focuses on preparing, routing, and signing documents. Startups that need reusable agreement templates, detailed internal approvals, structured contract data, or renewal tracking should compare it with contract management software. Startups that mainly exchange PDFs and already pay for Adobe products may find its familiar document workflow more useful than adding another standalone signing interface.


## **Dropbox Sign**


Dropbox Sign suits startups that need a focused signing tool without a broader contract management platform. Its straightforward interface supports common tasks such as uploading documents, adding signature fields, sending reminders, and maintaining an audit trail.


The API makes Dropbox Sign a practical option for startups that want to embed signatures into a product or automate requests through an existing application. Your developers can use the Dropbox Sign API to add signing to customer onboarding, approvals, or account workflows. Confirm the API plan, authentication options, and embedded-signing requirements before implementation.


Dropbox Sign works best when your contracts already exist as Word files, PDFs, or reusable templates. Startups that need internal approval routing, structured contract data, clause management, or renewal tracking may need separate tools around it. Buyers should compare plan limits, API access, template allowances, and integration availability because those details determine the actual cost at higher document volumes.


## **SignNow**


SignNow suits budget-conscious startups that need several people to prepare, send, and track signature requests. Its per-user tiers may suit startups that need several sender accounts. Compare the total annual cost, usage limits, and included features with equivalent plans from other providers.


The product covers common workflows such as reusable templates, signer roles, reminders, and document status tracking. Those capabilities fit routine sales agreements, hiring documents, and vendor forms when your main goal is collecting signatures rather than managing the full contract lifecycle.


Before choosing a plan, compare its integration access, audit trail detail, and administrative controls with your requirements. Lower tiers may place limits on certain features or usage. A startup with formal compliance reviews, complex approval routing, or extensive contract data needs may require a higher tier or separate contract management software. SignNow is best evaluated as a multi-user signing product rather than a full contract management platform.


## **Zoho Sign**


Zoho Sign fits startups that already manage customer records and documents in Zoho’s business apps. Connections with products such as Zoho CRM, Zoho Writer, and Zoho WorkDrive can reduce manual file transfers and keep signature requests inside familiar workflows.


Zoho Sign covers common e-signature needs such as templates, reminders, signing order, and audit trails. Zoho Sign is most relevant to startups that can connect signature requests with records and documents already stored in Zoho products. A startup using several Zoho products may find that convenience more valuable than adding a separate vendor.


Startups outside the Zoho suite should compare Zoho Sign with standalone tools based on plan limits, integrations, and document volume. Companies that need internal approvals, structured contract data, and renewal tracking may require contract management software beyond Zoho Sign’s core signing workflow.


## **Common Paper**


[Common Paper](https://commonpaper.com/) fits startups that want e-signatures inside a broader contract workflow. Sales representatives can send preapproved contracts from their CRM. Reviewers in legal, finance, or security can examine exceptions before signature.


Common Paper’s standard agreements give startups reusable foundations for documents such as mutual NDAs, cloud service agreements, and data processing agreements. Common Paper’s standard agreements are open source and maintained by a committee of attorneys. You can adapt them to your company’s terms or bring your own templates.


Gerri reviews Word and PDF contracts against company-defined playbooks. Gerri can propose redlines and route terms outside the playbook to the designated reviewer. Common Paper records the review history. Internal reviewers can focus on unusual terms instead of checking every clause manually.


Common Paper also stores contract terms as structured data that can flow into downstream systems such as Stripe and Zendesk. Systems such as billing and support tools can use structured contract fields without requiring someone to copy terms manually from the signed document.


A standalone e-signature product may suit a startup that mainly uploads documents, places signature fields, and tracks completion. Common Paper suits startups that also need reusable agreements, internal review, CRM-based sending, and accessible contract data after execution.


## **How to send a Word or PDF contract for signature**


1. Prepare the final document before adding signature fields. Resolve comments and tracked changes in Word, then confirm names, dates, payment terms, and signature blocks. Export the file as a PDF when you need to preserve fonts, spacing, and page breaks.
2. Choose between a static upload and a reusable template. A static PDF works well for an occasional agreement, but you must place fields again when the document changes. A structured template can preserve fields and contract data across repeated sales or hiring workflows.
3. Upload the document and assign each field to a recipient. Add fields for signatures, initials, and dates where needed. Some platforms use drag-and-drop fields, while others support tags embedded in the source document.
4. Set the signer order before sending. Sequential routing sends the document to each person after the prior signer finishes. Parallel routing lets everyone sign at the same time. Use sequential routing when an internal countersigner should sign only after the customer or employee.
5. Review the recipient emails and field assignments. Use the platform’s preview to confirm that every required field belongs to the correct signer, then send the request.


[Common Paper](https://commonpaper.com/) adds an optional review step before signature. Gerri can compare the same Word or PDF contract with your playbooks and propose redlines. It can then route exceptions to the designated reviewer.


## **Tracking unsigned documents and correcting signature requests**


A signing dashboard should show which requests remain unopened, viewed, or partially signed. Filters and notifications help you find stalled documents without checking each recipient manually. Common Paper tracks request status in a central workspace. Confirm which status events and filters each competing product includes at the plan you are considering.


Automated reminders reduce manual follow-up. Products may support scheduled reminders and request expiration dates, but availability and configuration vary by plan. Choose a cadence that matches the document. A sales contract may need faster follow-up than routine hiring paperwork.


Corrections depend on the error and the software. Some products let you update a recipient’s email address or reposition a field while the request remains open, but permissions vary by product and plan. A wrong attachment or changed contract language usually requires you to void the request, fix the document, and send a new version.


Voiding preserves a clear record that recipients should no longer sign the earlier request. After anyone has completed a signature, avoid modifying the signed file. Send a corrected agreement or amendment instead, and keep both records so the audit history remains clear.


## **Collecting countersignatures and multi-party approvals**


Set the signer order before sending a contract. For a sales agreement, a typical sequence routes the draft through legal or finance, sends it to the customer, and then requests a countersignature from an authorized executive. Hiring documents may require approval from finance before the candidate and company representative sign.


Keep internal approvals separate from legally significant signatures. Approval rules can route contracts based on deal size, payment terms, or changes to standard language. Common Paper supports this workflow through reusable agreements, company-defined review playbooks, and escalation of exceptions to the appropriate owner.


Manual coordination becomes unreliable as contract volume grows. Email threads and spreadsheets require someone to update approval and signature status manually. A shared contract workflow can record each step, trigger the next request, and display the current document status. A shared contract workflow records each step, sends the next request automatically, and gives you one place to check the agreement’s status.


## **Standalone e-signature vs. contract management software**


Standalone e-signature software fits when documents are infrequent and the work ends after everyone signs. If one person can prepare and route a PDF, and completed copies remain easy to find, a signature tool provides enough support.


Contract management becomes useful when volume makes manual follow-up unreliable. Consider switching when you send recurring agreements each week, maintain spreadsheets for renewal dates, or copy contract terms into other business tools. Structured contract data stores details such as payment terms and renewal dates separately from the document, which makes those details searchable and usable in other software.


Cross-functional review provides another trigger. Sales contracts may need finance approval for pricing or legal review for nonstandard language. A contract platform can route exceptions to the right owner and retain the approval history. Standalone tools usually focus on document delivery, signer authentication, and completion records.


Evaluate the signing, approval, and post-signature work you expect over the next year. Keep standalone software if signing remains occasional and nobody needs to track obligations after signature. Consider[Common Paper](https://commonpaper.com/) when reusable agreements, internal approvals, and structured contract data need to share one workflow. Common Paper supports CRM-based sending and contract status tracking, while structured data can flow into downstream systems. Smart Playbooks can review Word and PDF contracts before signature and send exceptions to the appropriate owner.


Contract management software extends beyond electronic signatures to cover drafting, review, approval, and post-signature tracking. Consider it when those tasks require manual coordination outside the signing product.


## **FAQs**


- **Is a free e-signature tool legally binding?** The price of a tool does not impact whether e-signatures are legally binding. Enforceability depends on the applicable law, the parties’ intent and consent, the signed record, and any formal requirements for that contract type. Consult qualified legal counsel for regulated transactions or agreements with special execution requirements.
- **What counts as an audit trail?** An audit trail records events such as when the sender issued the document, when each signer opened and signed it, and which email address or authentication method they used. Strong audit trails also preserve timestamps, document history, and a completion certificate.
- **Can you send a contract for signature without creating an account?** Sender account requirements vary by provider and workflow. Signers can often use an emailed link without creating an account, although identity verification may require additional steps. Signers can often review and sign through an emailed link without registering, though identity checks may add extra steps.
- **How many signers can typical plans support?** The products in this guide may support multiple signers, sequential signing, and countersignatures, but recipient limits and feature availability vary by plan. Exact recipient limits, monthly document allowances, and bulk-send access depend on the provider and plan.


## **Conclusion**


Choose electronic signature software based on your current contract volume and the number of people who will participate in contracting over the next year. A simple signing tool can cover occasional documents when one person prepares, sends, and tracks each request. Consider contract management when recurring agreements require shared approvals, structured contract data, or post-signature tracking.[Common Paper](https://commonpaper.com/) is designed for startups reaching that stage, while a standalone signing tool remains appropriate for occasional documents. Choose the smallest product category that supports the workflow you expect over the next year.
